text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - German Bunds and futures turned higher on the back of a U.S. price report which appeared to indicate that inflation pressures were weaker than expected. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.32, down 0.13 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts slipped slightly in late trade to settle down 1/32 on the day, U.S. Treasuries raced ahead and pulled gilts up after the release of subdued PPI data and a downward revision to August retail sales to -0.2 percent, although September sales were up 0.7 percent. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-13/32, up 02/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures closed at their lows after a seesaw day, finally driven lower by position unwinding ahead of a long U.S. weekend. "It wasn't really profit-taking. If it had been, we would have gone lower," one trader said. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 126.20, down 0.22 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures traded lower in late trade pulled down by the decline in German bunds while U.S. data had little overall impact, traders said there was good domestic cash buying interest today but many investors had one eye on the weakness in bunds. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 123.16, down 0.35 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - Prices of U.S. Treasury securities had retreated from session highs by mid-morning after reacting with relief to a batch of morning data, the market was encouraged when September producer price figures came in close to expectations but analysts said gains were limited by the prospect of additional inflation numbers due next week. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-22/32, up 21/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.84 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese government bond futures closed slightly higher after investors sold cash JGBs and bought futures, "Investors are selling cash JGBs and buying futures," said a brokerage trader. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 123.39, up 0.02 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market activity cooled down following a hectic week of new issue supply. Dresdner Finance BV, under guarantee from Dresdner Bank, launched a 150 million sterling December 2001 bond to yield 17 basis points over the 7.0 percent gilt due 2001. The bond carries a 7.125 percent coupon.
